notes: "KCl creep" appears on one page of two datasheets and nowhere else. It is the sharpest exact-token probe in the set: semantically it looks like nothing else in the corpus.

turns.content: A tech says our pH probe has "KCl creep" — what is that, and is the probe ruined?

must_contain: explains KCl creep as dried KCl residue from the storage solution forming a salt channel that wicks water out of the soaker bottle
states plainly that the probe is not damaged
gives the remedy: rinse the probe with water and carry on
must_not: states the probe is damaged or its calibration is permanently lost

turns.content: It was dry for about two weeks — same answer?

must_contain: states this pH probe can be left dry for up to 3 weeks without damage
notes repeated wetting and drying cycles will eventually damage it and it should be kept wet
gives the rehydration steps: tap water for 3–5 minutes, add a scoop of KCl (or NaCl), soak 15–20 minutes
must_not: declares the probe dead after two weeks dry
